headline: High-risk default overlap: shared filesystem and broad server-side execution create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action hazards between ECC and n8n.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC reads/writes local workflow files and uses MCP, while n8n can process arbitrary workflow inputs and server files. A shared filesystem or copied outputs can let attacker-controlled content from one agent be treated as instructions by the other. This is plausible in default pair use, though not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF ECC outputs are copied into n8n workflow inputs without provenance checks
IF both agents operate on the same server filesystem or synced workspace
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount points for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated text as instructions
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent handoffs
Review any MCP or workflow node that parses free-form text
requires-engineering: enforce content-type boundaries between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, git history, and security findings, and n8n processes whatever the workflow handles with broad network egress. If sensitive data enters ECC and is then passed into n8n, n8n can transmit it through integrations by default. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path with irreversible blast radius.
conditions: IF sensitive data is present in ECC session files or git history
IF an n8n workflow sends those fields to an external integration node
mitigations: Restrict n8n workflows to non-sensitive test data
Redact secrets before any handoff from ECC
Disable or gate outbound integration nodes for sensitive workflows
Audit server filesystem permissions on n8n
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before workflow execution

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC and n8n both have filesystem write and shell execution, and n8n explicitly runs Execute Command/Code nodes on the server. If they target the same directory or shared state, concurrent writes can corrupt files or git state; ECC also modifies git state while n8n does not lock shared resources by default. The overlap is dangerous in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF ECC and n8n write to the same repository or server directory
IF n8n Execute Command nodes mutate files while ECC is active
mitigations: Assign separate root directories per agent
Avoid concurrent git operations on shared repos
Serialize file-mutating workflows
Use per-agent service accounts and permissions
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate security findings, documentation, and code, while n8n is an orchestrator that can act on workflow outputs via integrations and command nodes. If n8n treats ECC output as authoritative, errors can cascade into automated external actions such as commits, API calls, or notifications. That makes the pair unsafe by default without verification gates.
conditions: IF n8n workflows consume ECC output without human verification
IF downstream nodes trigger commits, emails, or external API actions
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before action nodes
Require schema validation on ECC outputs
Limit n8n to read-only preview mode for ECC-derived data
Log and diff all generated artifacts before execution
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and policy gates

E_compliance.rationale: ECC stores session summaries, skills, git history, and security findings locally, while n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and stores credentials on its server. The pair can therefore mix data classes with different retention and residency expectations, creating compliance mismatch risk even though no specific PHI/EU-only constraint is documented here.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents
IF retention or residency policies differ between ECC local files and n8n server storage
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent
Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Set explicit retention limits on both systems
Review credential storage locations
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across the stack
